key_insight: The paper mines 38 AI-generated math families to extract reusable “mathematical instruments” such as lemmas, constructions, inequalities, and proof mechanisms, rather than just judging theorems.
engineering_relevance: It offers a structured way to turn large-language-model mathematical outputs into candidate building blocks for theorem proving, formalization workflows, and automated discovery pipelines.
method: Surveyed 38 problem families across two groups spanning number theory, geometry, analysis, combinatorics, complexity, algebra, operator algebras, topology, and mathematical physics.
Recorded for each entry the claim, extracted instruments, antecedents, and caveats.
Added cross-cutting patterns plus a scoreboard of formalization status and dependencies.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a corpus of 722 AI-written manuscripts organized into 372 problem families, with selected source comparisons used to correct statements, hypotheses, and counts.
watch_item: Novelty and correctness assessments are explicitly provisional, and no Lean development was compiled or kernel-checked, so the extracted instruments should not be treated as verified proofs.
paper_title: What the Machine Invented: Mining New Mathematical Instruments from OpenAI's October 2026 Release of AI-Generated Mathematics
